# 1 Enoch Chapter 63 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** In those days the powerful and the kings who rule the earth will beg for a brief reprieve from the punishment-angels to whom they have been handed over — just enough time to fall down and worship before the Lord of Spirits and confess their sins in his presence.

**2** They will bless and glorify the Lord of Spirits and say: "Blessed is the Lord of Spirits, Lord of kings, Lord of the powerful and Lord of the wealthy, Lord of glory and Lord of wisdom.

**3** Every secret is laid bare before you. Your power endures through every generation, and your glory lasts forever and ever. Your secrets are deep and countless and beyond investigation; your righteousness is beyond calculation.

**4** We have finally learned that we should have glorified and blessed the Lord of kings — the one who is king above all kings.

**5** If only we had rest to glorify and give thanks and declare our faith before his glory! But now we desperately want even a moment of rest and cannot find it; we chase after it and it escapes us. The light has gone out in front of us, and darkness is our home forever and ever.

**6** For we never believed in him, never glorified the name of the Lord of Spirits. Our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom and in our own glory.

**7** On the day of our suffering and distress he does not rescue us. We find no breathing space to confess that our Lord is just in all his works and his judgments and his justice — that he shows no favoritism in his judgments.

**8** We are driven away from before his face because of what we have done, and all our sins are being counted out in righteousness against us.

**9** Then they will say to one another: 'Our whole being is filled with the profits of injustice, but that won't stop us from sinking into the weight of Sheol.'"

**10** After that, their faces will fill with darkness and shame before that Son of Man, and they will be expelled from his presence, while the sword stands ready before his face in the middle of them.

**11** This was the declaration of the Lord of Spirits: "This is the ordinance and the verdict for the powerful and the kings and the arrogant and those who own the earth — before the Lord of Spirits."

**12** And I saw other shapes hidden in that place. I heard the angel's voice saying: "These are the angels who came down to earth and exposed hidden things to humanity, and drew human beings into sin."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Ch. 63's prayer of the kings is one of the most theologically charged passages in the Parables — a complete repentance that comes too late and is explicitly rejected. V. 6 ('our hope was in the scepter') is the definitive verdict on imperial power. V. 9 ('souls full of unrighteous gain') is a sharp social critique echoing the prophets. V. 12 reconnects to the Watcher mythology of ch. 6-16.*
